synopsis: India’s DGMS circulars use Coal Mines Regulations 2017 regulation 216(2) as their regulatory hook; Circular No. 03 of 2024, dated 21 August 2024, calls for proximity-warning or anti-collision devices on wheeled trackless transportation machinery in opencast coal mines [f2301, f2302, f15587]. A 2025 technical circular calls for fail-safe braking before relevant tippers are deployed, while a 2025 Springer article cites an Indian circular setting a maximum speed of 30 km/h [f2303, f2455, f2304]. These are official guidance and enforcement materials, not evidence of a universal automatic-braking requirement for Indian construction machines; the regional survey found a hard automatic-braking mandate only in South Africa [f2306, f15073]. For planning, DGMS expectations form a site-specific acceptance gate beyond market-access validation and OEM testing, so collision mitigation should be configurable to meet those expectations [f2931, f2594, f15597]. Confidence in the circular details is low because the booklet relied on secondary summaries; it found neither a standardised national mine-interaction test matrix nor a dedicated off-road rule requiring a specified ML validation standard by 2028 [f2307, f2453, f2393].
